description: skills.listSkills over the skills Draggy ships (electron/skills-library), as the app lists them, with folder paths left out. It is the real corpus, so it changes when the library does: regenerate from the reference. Input: {}. Expected: the listing sorted by name.

cases.name: the shipped library lists every skill with its name, summary, shelf, side and switch

expected.name: accessibility
expected.description: Audits and fixes web interfaces for accessibility (semantic HTML, keyboard use, focus, labels, contrast, ARIA used correctly, screen reader announcements) against WCAG 2.2 AA. Use when the user asks for an accessibility review, a11y fixes, or to make a component usable with a keyboard or screen reader.

expected.name: add-feature
expected.description: Implements a new feature end to end in an existing project: understands the codebase, plans visible steps, follows existing patterns, writes the code and tests, and verifies it works. Use when the user asks to add, build or implement functionality in their project.
expected.summary: Build a feature end to end

expected.name: api-design
expected.description: Designs or reviews HTTP APIs (REST or JSON-RPC style) and GraphQL schemas: resources and naming, methods and status codes, errors, pagination, versioning, validation and consistency with the existing API. Use when the user is creating endpoints, designing an API, or wants an API reviewed.

expected.name: blog-post
expected.description: Plans and writes blog posts and articles with a strong headline, a hook, a logical structure, concrete examples and a clear takeaway. Use when the user wants an article, blog post, newsletter piece or long-form post drafted or outlined.
expected.summary: Write a blog post or article

expected.name: brainstorm
expected.description: Generates many varied ideas for names, projects, gifts, content, solutions or strategies, then helps narrow them down with clear criteria. Use when the user asks for ideas, options, suggestions, names or a brainstorm.

expected.name: browser-tasks
expected.description: Uses Draggy's live browser tools to get through pages that need clicking, typing, searching or scrolling, such as finding a timetable, checking availability or extracting a table. Use when read_url is not enough because the page is interactive.

expected.name: budget-planner
expected.description: Builds personal or household budgets from income and expenses, shows where money goes, suggests realistic savings and saves the budget as a spreadsheet. Use when the user wants to make a budget, track spending, save for something, or understand their finances.

expected.name: changelog
expected.description: Writes release notes and changelog entries from git history since the last release, grouped for readers (added, changed, fixed, breaking) and in the project's existing changelog format. Use when the user prepares a release, asks for release notes, or wants the changelog updated.

expected.name: ci-workflow
expected.description: Creates or fixes continuous integration workflows (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI) that install, lint, type-check, test and build the project reliably, with caching, a version matrix and minimal permissions. Use when the user wants CI set up, a workflow fixed, or a failing pipeline diagnosed.

expected.name: code-review
expected.description: Reviews uncommitted changes, a branch or given files for real bugs first (logic errors, edge cases, security, data loss), then maintainability, with specific, ranked findings. Use when the user asks for a code review, to check their changes, or whether something is ready to commit or merge.

expected.name: commit-message
expected.description: Writes clear commit messages from the actual staged or unstaged diff, following the project's existing convention (Conventional Commits, one-line style or other), and can make the commit. Use when the user asks for a commit message or to commit their changes.

expected.name: compare-options
expected.description: Compares products, services, tools or choices side by side against the criteria that matter to the user, with a scored table and a clear recommendation. Use when the user is deciding between options, asks which of two things to pick, or wants the best choice for their needs.

expected.name: cover-letter
expected.description: Writes tailored cover letters that connect the candidate's real experience to a specific job posting, in under a page. Use when the user wants a cover letter or motivation letter for a job, internship or programme.

expected.name: csv-cleaner
expected.description: Cleans messy tabular data: fixes headers, trims and normalises values, standardises dates and numbers, removes duplicates and flags invalid rows, reporting every change. Use when the user has a messy CSV, spreadsheet export or list that needs tidying before use.

expected.name: data-analysis
expected.description: Analyses tabular data such as CSV, spreadsheets and exports: cleans it, computes the right statistics exactly, finds patterns and explains what they mean without overclaiming. Use when the user shares data and asks for analysis, trends, totals, comparisons or insights.

expected.name: database-migration
expected.description: Plans and writes database schema migrations that are safe on existing data and running systems: expand-and-contract steps, backfills, indexes without locking, and a tested rollback. Use when the user needs to change a database schema, add or rename columns or tables, or migrate data.

expected.name: debugging
expected.description: Finds the root cause of a bug or failing test systematically (reproduce, read the error, form and test hypotheses, fix the cause not the symptom, and prove it with a test). Use when something is broken, a test fails, there is an error or stack trace, or behaviour is unexpected.
expected.summary: Find the cause of a bug

expected.name: dependency-upgrade
expected.description: Upgrades project dependencies safely: finds outdated and vulnerable packages, reads changelogs for breaking changes, upgrades in small batches, fixes the code and runs the tests after each. Use when the user wants to update packages, fix vulnerable dependencies, or move to a new major version of a library or framework.

expected.name: dockerfile
expected.description: Containerises applications with small, secure, cache-friendly Dockerfiles (multi-stage builds, pinned bases, non-root users, health checks) and a docker-compose file for local development when useful. Use when the user wants to dockerise a project, fix a Dockerfile, or speed up or slim down image builds.

expected.name: document-qa
expected.description: Answers questions from the user's own indexed documents using search_library, quoting the passages and naming the files the answer came from. Use when the user asks about their notes, files, contracts, manuals or anything in folders they added to the library.

expected.name: documentation
expected.description: Writes or updates project documentation (README, usage guides, API docs, docstrings and code comments) that is accurate to the code and matches the project's style. Use when the user asks to document code, write a README, or update docs after a change.

expected.name: docx
expected.description: Creates Word documents (.docx) with create_file from structured HTML (for custom styling, tables, colors and fonts) or Markdown. Use whenever the user asks for a Word document, a .docx, or an editable document to download.

expected.name: email-writer
expected.description: Drafts and replies to emails that get read and answered: a clear subject, the point in the first lines, and a tone that fits the reader. Use when the user wants an email written, answered, shortened or made more polite.

expected.name: explain-codebase
expected.description: Gives a guided tour of an unfamiliar project: what it does, how it is organised, the main flows through the code, how to run and test it, and where to start for a given task. Use when the user is new to a codebase or asks how a project or part of it works.

expected.name: explain-concept
expected.description: Explains a concept, idea or process at the right level for the learner, building from what they know with plain language, analogies, examples and a quick check of understanding. Use when the user asks what something is, how it works, or to explain it simply.

expected.name: fact-check
expected.description: Checks whether a claim, quote, statistic, image caption or viral post is true, using primary sources where possible, and gives a clear verdict with evidence. Use when the user asks whether something is true, wants something verified, or shares a suspicious claim.
expected.summary: Check whether a claim is true

expected.name: flashcards
expected.description: Turns notes, chapters, vocabulary lists or a topic into effective flashcards (one fact per card, clear cues) and saves them as a spreadsheet ready to import into Anki or Quizlet. Use when the user asks for flashcards, study cards or Anki cards.

expected.name: formal-letter
expected.description: Writes formal letters (complaints, requests, resignations, notices, letters to authorities or landlords) with the correct layout and firm, polite language, saved as Word or PDF. Use when the user needs an official or formal letter rather than an email.

expected.name: frontend-design
expected.description: Architect and build high-end, human-crafted web interfaces in Draggy: eliminates AI aesthetic tropes, establishes editorial and engineering pedigree, and enforces strict typographic, spatial, and interaction standards.

expected.name: git-helper
expected.description: Helps with git beyond basic commits: resolving merge conflicts, rebasing, undoing mistakes, recovering lost work, cleaning history and understanding what happened, always with safe, explained commands. Use when the user has a git problem or asks how to do something in git.

expected.name: goal-planner
expected.description: Turns a personal or professional goal into specific milestones, weekly habits, obstacles planned for and a simple way to track progress. Use when the user wants to set goals, build a habit, plan a change or stay accountable.
expected.summary: Turn a goal into a plan

expected.name: human
expected.description: Comprehensive editorial specification based on Wikipedia's Signs of AI Writing (WP:AISIGNS) to eliminate LLM stylistic tells, structural cliches, synthetic commentary, uniform cadence, and formatting artifacts. Use whenever generating, rewriting, auditing, or polishing any text intended to read as authentic, authoritative human prose.

expected.name: invoice
expected.description: Prepares invoices and quotes with numbered line items, correct arithmetic, tax, totals and payment details, as a PDF to send and a spreadsheet of the lines if wanted. Use when the user asks for an invoice, a quote, an estimate or a bill.

expected.name: language-tutor
expected.description: Acts as a patient language tutor: conversation practice at the learner's level, gentle corrections with explanations, vocabulary building and short exercises. Use when the user wants to practise or learn a language, or asks for corrections of their writing in a language they are learning.

expected.name: literature-review
expected.description: Finds and synthesises academic and scientific sources on a research question, summarising methods, findings, agreement, gaps and quality, with proper citations. Use when the user needs a literature review, the state of research on a topic, or evidence from studies.

expected.name: meal-planner
expected.description: Plans meals for a week or more around diets, allergies, budget, cooking time and leftovers, with recipes outlines and a shopping list grouped by aisle. Use when the user wants a meal plan, weekly menu, batch cooking plan or shopping list.

expected.name: meeting-notes
expected.description: Turns meeting transcripts, recordings' text or rough notes into clean minutes with decisions, action items with owners and dates, and open questions. Use when the user shares meeting notes or a transcript, or asks for minutes or a recap.

expected.name: news-brief
expected.description: Gathers the latest news on a topic, company, country or event from several outlets and writes a dated briefing with what happened, why it matters and what to watch. Use when the user asks what is new, the latest on something, or for a news roundup.
expected.summary: Catch up on the latest news

expected.name: pdf
expected.description: Creates polished PDF documents with create_file from styled HTML (for custom fonts, colors, tables and layouts) or Markdown. Use whenever the user asks for a PDF, a printable document, a handout or a report to send.

expected.name: performance
expected.description: Finds and fixes performance problems by measuring first: profiles or times the slow path, identifies the real bottleneck (algorithm, I/O, queries, rendering, memory) and verifies the improvement with numbers. Use when code is slow, uses too much memory, or the user asks to optimise something.

expected.name: pptx
expected.description: Creates PowerPoint slide decks (.pptx) with create_file from styled HTML (with background colors, tables, and custom fonts) or Markdown. Use whenever the user asks for slides, a presentation, a deck or a .pptx file.

expected.name: project-plan
expected.description: Turns a goal into a project plan: scope, milestones, tasks with owners and estimates, dependencies, risks and a timeline, saved as a spreadsheet or document. Use when the user needs to plan a project, an event, a launch, a move or any multi-step undertaking.

expected.name: proofreader
expected.description: Corrects spelling, grammar, punctuation and awkward phrasing while keeping the author's voice and meaning, then lists what changed. Use when the user asks to proofread, check, correct or polish a text.

expected.name: pull-request
expected.description: Writes pull request descriptions from the branch's real diff and commits (summary, why, changes, testing, risks, screenshots to add) and can open the PR with the GitHub CLI. Use when the user asks for a PR description or to open a pull request.

expected.name: quiz-me
expected.description: Runs an interactive quiz on any topic or on material the user provides, one question at a time, adapting difficulty and explaining every answer. Use when the user wants to be quizzed, tested, or to practise for an exam.

expected.name: refactor
expected.description: Improves the structure of existing code without changing its behaviour, in small verified steps: extracting functions, removing duplication, clarifying names, simplifying conditionals. Use when the user asks to refactor, clean up, simplify, or restructure code.

expected.name: regex-helper
expected.description: Builds, explains and tests regular expressions for a given flavour (JavaScript, Python, PCRE, .NET, grep), with examples that should and should not match. Use when the user needs a regex, wants one explained, or a pattern is not matching as expected.

expected.name: report
expected.description: Writes structured reports (executive summary, findings, analysis, recommendations) from notes, data or research, and saves them as Word or PDF. Use when the user asks for a report, a written analysis, a status update document or a briefing paper.

expected.name: resume
expected.description: Builds and improves CVs and résumés: achievement-focused bullet points, a clear layout, tailoring to a target role, and a Word or PDF file. Use when the user wants a CV or résumé written, reviewed, tailored or turned into a document.

expected.name: security-review
expected.description: Audits code or pending changes for security vulnerabilities (injection, broken access control, secrets, unsafe file and command handling, dependency risks) with evidence, severity and fixes. Use when the user asks for a security review, audit, or whether code is safe.

expected.name: shell-script
expected.description: Writes robust shell scripts for bash, PowerShell or cmd, with safe quoting, error handling, dry-run options and clear usage, and explains commands before anything destructive. Use when the user wants a script to automate a task, a one-liner explained, or a script fixed.

expected.name: skill-creator
expected.description: Helps the user write a new skill in the SKILL.md format: a precise name and trigger description, clear step-by-step instructions, examples and optional bundled files, saved where Draggy will find it. Use when the user wants to create, improve or test a skill, or teach Draggy how they like a job done.

expected.name: social-post
expected.description: Writes posts for LinkedIn, X, Instagram, Mastodon, Bluesky and similar, fitted to each platform's length, style and hashtag habits, with a hook in the first line. Use when the user wants a social media post, thread or caption.

expected.name: speech-writer
expected.description: Writes speeches, toasts, presentations' spoken script and talks meant to be heard rather than read, timed to a target length. Use when the user needs a wedding toast, keynote, eulogy, pitch, team talk or any text to be spoken aloud.

expected.name: spreadsheet-formulas
expected.description: Writes and explains Excel, Google Sheets and LibreOffice formulas (lookups, conditional sums, dates, text, array formulas and pivot-style summaries) and fixes formula errors. Use when the user asks how to calculate something in a spreadsheet or has a formula that returns an error.

expected.name: sql-helper
expected.description: Writes, explains, debugs and optimises SQL queries for PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, SQL Server and others, with correct joins, grouping and safe parameterisation. Use when the user needs a SQL query, has a query error, or wants a query explained or made faster.

expected.name: story-writer
expected.description: Writes fiction: short stories, scenes, bedtime stories, fan fiction and creative prompts, with vivid characters, a real arc and the requested style and length. Use when the user asks for a story, a scene, a poem-like narrative or creative writing help.

expected.name: study-plan
expected.description: Builds a realistic study or learning plan toward an exam, certification or skill, with weekly goals, spaced review, practice tests and a calendar-friendly schedule. Use when the user wants to plan studying, prepare for an exam, or learn a skill by a date.

expected.name: summarizer
expected.description: Condenses articles, documents, transcripts, threads and web pages into faithful summaries at the length the user needs, keeping key numbers, decisions and caveats. Use when the user asks for a summary, TL;DR, key points or the gist of something.

expected.name: tone-rewriter
expected.description: Rewrites a text for a different tone, audience or length (more formal, friendlier, more confident, simpler, shorter) while keeping every fact and intent. Use when the user asks to make something sound different or fit a new reader.

expected.name: translator
expected.description: Translates text between languages faithfully and naturally, keeping formatting, tone, names and technical terms, and flagging idioms or ambiguities. Use when the user asks to translate something or wants it in another language.

expected.name: trip-planner
expected.description: Plans trips with a day-by-day itinerary, realistic travel times, bookings to make, a budget estimate and a packing list, saved as a printable PDF if wanted. Use when the user is planning a holiday, weekend away, business trip or route.

expected.name: type-errors
expected.description: Fixes type errors and strengthens typing in TypeScript, Python (mypy, pyright) and similar, by finding the real mismatch rather than silencing it with any, casts or ignore comments. Use when the type checker fails, the user asks to add types, or to remove any and unsafe casts.

expected.name: web-research
expected.description: Researches a question across several web sources with search_web and read_url, cross-checks what they say, and answers with inline citations and a source list. Use when the user asks to research, look into, find out about or investigate something that needs current or detailed information.

expected.name: write-tests
expected.description: Adds meaningful automated tests using the project's existing framework and conventions, covering behaviour, edge cases and regressions, and runs them. Use when the user asks for tests, better coverage, or a test for a bug or new feature.

expected.name: xlsx
expected.description: Creates Excel spreadsheets (.xlsx) with create_file from styled HTML tables (with custom column widths, colors, borders and numbers) or clean CSV. Use whenever the user asks for a spreadsheet, an Excel file, a table to download, or data in .xlsx.
